newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says it defused 352,000 allied bombs.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says it defused 352,000 allied bombs.

text.p: Iraqi newspapers said on Monday civil defence teams had so far defused more than 352,000 bombs since the end of the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
The papers said the bombs were of different sizes and kinds and ranged from cluster shells to unexploded cruise missiles.

"Civil defence teams defused or treated 181,812 bombs of different types and sizes in 1991, 38,532 in 1992, 34,484 in 1993, 19,255 in 1994, 54,888 in 1995 and 23,402 in 1996," the papers said quoting a civil defence source.

The source said Iraqi civil defence teams were still active in the search for bombs dropped "by the vicious 30-state aggression," a reference to the U.S.-led multinational force which ejected Iraqi troops from Kuwait in 1991.
He said Iraq's civil defence was holding seminars and lectures instructing ordinary citizens how to avoid the bombs when coming across them.

In the past Iraq reported the death of several people, including women and children, as a result of the explosion of bombs the allies dropped during their massive air campaign to force Iraq to withdraw its troops from Kuwait which it occupied in 1990.
